scan.timestamp_policy: No wall-clock timestamp is embedded so repeated scans of unchanged source are byte-identical.
scan.root_policy: Only the directory name is recorded; all paths in this report are relative to the scan root.
limitations: Only requirements*.txt, pyproject.toml, setup.cfg and setup.py (literal values) are parsed; Pipfile, poetry/pdm tables, conda files and lockfiles are not.
setup.py is analyzed statically and never executed; computed dependency lists are not evaluated.
Constraint files (-c) and remote includes are noted but not compared.
Compatibility of two specifiers is judged against a bounded set of candidate versions; when the result cannot be proven the finding is reported as uncertain.
Different or incompatible constraints are observations, not proof of runtime failure, and no security advisory data is consulted.
No manifests found means the repository was not assessed, not that it is clean.

limitations: Import-to-distribution mappings come from metadata installed in the Python environment running this tool; uninstalled distributions fall back to a name-based guess and are labelled mapping_unavailable when unmatched.
Dynamic imports with non-literal targets, plugin loading, entry points, runtime loading, CLI-only use, data-only packages and optional features cannot be detected statically.
Literal importlib.import_module('x') / __import__('x') calls are recorded as kind=dynamic_literal.
A missing import must never be treated as proof that a package is unused; do not remove packages on this basis.
Import roots are matched at top level only; namespace packages shared by several distributions may over-match.
